## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

``` [arch@nightly-essarch-org ~]$ cat tasks.py from celery import Celery, chain, group app = Celery('tasks', backend='db+sqlite:///results.sqlite', broker='amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5672') @app.task() def prepare(): print("Prepare work!") @app.task() def foop1(): print("this is from foop1!") @app.task() def foop2(): print("this is from foop2!") @app.task() def foop2_post(): print("this is from foop2 post!") @app.task() def finish(): print("Finish, all work done!") @app.task() def fail(): raise ValueError("this is from fail!") if __name__ == '__main__': workflow_ok = chain(prepare.si(), group(foop1.si(), chain(foop1.si(), group(foop2.si(), foop2.si()), foop2_post.si())), finish.si()) workflow_fail = chain(prepare.si(), group(foop1.si(), chain(fail.si(), group(foop2.si(), foop2.si()), foop2_post.si())), finish.si()) print('workflow ok: {}'.format(workflow_ok)) workflow_ok.delay() print('workflow fail: {}'.format(workflow_fail)) workflow_fail.delay() ``` ``` [arch@nightly-essarch-org ~]$ python tasks.py workflow ok: tasks.prepare() | %finish((foop1(), foop1() | %foop2_post((foop2(), foop2())))) workflow fail: tasks.prepare() | %finish((foop1(), fail() | %foop2_post((foop2(), foop2())))) ```

# Expected Behavior I'm not sure what the intended behavior of chord_unlock is here but I feel that its current behavior atleast isn't consistent. The test case I've provided above results in what I've included below in Actual Behavior where it gets stuck in an infinite loop with chord_unlock.
